summary: Runtime validation confirms planner-only orchestration, monitor contract, frontend, cron ownership, and critical endpoint contract are live after the DEV-03 chain. A bounded runtime patch was applied to stop accepting You.com auth-wall text as a successful LLM answer, but `/api/copilot/ask` still falls back to the degraded memo path, so the personal finance copilot remains user-visibly blocked on live memo generation.
root_cause: The judge/copilot runtime treated provider auth-wall HTML as a successful LLM reply. After rejecting that invalid response, the backend still cannot produce a non-fallback memo from the remaining provider chain, so the ask surface continues to degrade to `model=fallback`.
fix_applied: Patched `domains.judge.application.g4f_client` to detect auth-wall/login/pricing responses and continue to the next provider instead of returning unusable content; added regression coverage for fast-path and ranked-candidate auth-wall fallback behavior; restarted the Finance Copilot runtime.

architecture_check: Bounded runtime/control-plane change only: no queue/workboard mutation, no frontend/theme change, no repo-wide planner behavior change. The patch is isolated to provider-response validation in the shared judge/copilot LLM bridge and preserves DEV-03 surface contracts.
vision_alignment: Aligned with the product goal because it removes one false-success path on the `brief + ask` runtime and keeps proof focused on the user-visible memo generation path instead of broad orchestration changes.
recommended_next: Planner should route the remaining blocker to dev/runtime for the next bounded fix: inspect why the post-auth-wall provider chain still cannot produce a non-fallback memo for `/api/copilot/ask` and capture the exact provider/error from the judge bridge during a live ask.
blocking_issue: BATCH-69 remains blocked on live copilot memo generation: `/api/copilot/ask` still degrades to `model=fallback` after the auth-wall guard, so the ask surface does not yet meet the user-visible investment memo requirement.
